data.gender_notes: Asyura is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Arabic name Asyura is derived from the Arabic word 'asyurah' which means 'ten [days] of fasting'. It refers to the tenth day of Muharram in the Islamic lunar calendar, which is a day of commemoration and reflection for Muslims around the world. The name Asyura carries the meaning “Ten [days] of fasting” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Asyura usually hope their child will grow to embody ten [days] of fasting and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of self-discipline, sacrifice, and spiritual growth, Asyura is a name that embodies the essence of the Islamic faith.
data.etymology: Asyura belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ten [days] of fasting.”

in_english.name: Asyura
in_english.meaning: Tenth day of Muharram, day of mourning and grief
in_english.long_meaning: Asyura, also known as Ashura, refers to the tenth day of the Islamic month of Muharram. It holds great significance in Islamic tradition, particularly for Shia Muslims, as it commemorates the martyrdom of Imam Hussein, a grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, in the Battle of Karbala. This event is a pivotal moment in Islamic history, symbolizing the struggle between good and evil. On this day, many Muslims, especially Shia communities, observe mourning rituals, including processions, lamentations, and reenactments of the Battle of Karbala, to express their grief and solidarity with the Ahl al-Bayt (the family of the Prophet Muhammad)

data.cultural_impact: Asyura marks the anniversary of the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad, in the Battle of Karbala. It is a day of remembrance and mourning for the Shia Muslim community. Traditions include expressing empathy, give Zakat and Kaffarah, visits to Imam Hussain’s shrine, and communal gatherings for commemoration meals and processions.
data.spiritual_significance: Asyura is a day of spiritual reflection and repentance for Muslims. It is a time to seek forgiveness from Allah, strengthen faith, and build good deeds and virtues through acts of charity and self-discipline. The fasting and devotional practices of this day remind Muslims of the sacrifices and hardships faced by Prophet Ibrahim and Imam Hussein, and inspire them to strive for a closer relationship with Allah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The day of Ashura signifies the triumph of faith and sacrifice over worldly desires and temptations. It marks the commemoration of Prophet Hussein's (as) supreme sacrifice, reminding us of the importance of self-discipline and steadfastness in the face of adversity.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The Day of Ashura marked the end of the 40-day period of mourning for the Prophet Muhammad's grandson, Imam Hussein, who was killed in the Battle of Karbala in 61 AH (680 AD).
historical_references.context: Mourning for Imam Hussein's death and commemorating his martyrdom

historical_references.reference: During the early Islamic period, the Day of Ashura was also observed by the Jews as a day of fasting and mourning for the destruction of the First Temple in Jerusalem in 586 BC.
historical_references.context: Communally observing the Jewish practice and showing solidarity with their religious communities

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic holiday of Ashura, marking the martyrdom of Imam Husain ibn Ali and commemorating his sacrifice, is observed by millions of Muslims around the world. Modern practices include fasting, visiting the graves of loved ones or Islamic figures, and expressing devotion on social media platforms. The day is also marked with solemn processions and remembrance gatherings, where individuals come together to mourn the sacrifices made during this significant period in Islamic history.
